text:
erin: Quick sync  - execs asked for a single canonical playbook for cross-region degradation + tenant isolation impacts. Need a short decision for roadmap grooming.

samir: Short list of asks from sales: clear customer-facing semantics for 'regional degrade' (what we failover to), a simple cost/SLA summary, and a safe migration checklist.

zoe: Ops perspective: two separate problems: (A) proactive routing rules for jurisdiction/residency, and (B) reactive degradation behavior when regions hit capacity or partial outage. We should treat them separately but expose one policy surface.

carlo: Proposal: policy layers = [residency_lock, tenancy_affinity, degradation_chain]. Degradation chain is an ordered list, e.g. [quantized_same_region, compatible_model_same_region, compatible_model_other_region, reject]. We'll document default and per-tenant overrides.

erin: Important nuance: some EU customers require both residency_lock AND no cross-region fallback. Default policy should be residency_lock=true, allow_cross_region_fallback=false unless explicitly opted-in.

samir: Sales request: one-line matrix for customers: if they want cross-region fallback tick box, note cost delta and potential latency impact. Also need sample contract clause that specifies whether we can fall back in emergencies.

zoe: Ops notes on implementation: routing decisions must be deterministic and idempotent. Include a route_decision_hash in response headers and log the fallback step chosen. Also preserve request-level metadata so canary rollbacks are simpler.

carlo: Rough infra work: (1) policy engine precedence + per-tenant override ~3w, (2) fallback chain runtime + trace headers ~3w, (3) residency verification + KMS opt-in hooks ~2w, (4) billing hook for SLA-breach credits ~2w. End-to-end MVP ~8w if parallelized.

erin: Can we make a small MVP that unblocks sales? My thought: implement residency_lock + a safe default degradation chain that disallows cross-region fallback. That would let us close many EU pilots quickly.

samir: Agree. If we disallow cross-region by default we can offer a paid opt-in for higher availability that permits cross-region fallback and shows estimated cost.

zoe: Ops gating checklist for MVP: residency verification test (data-in-region), KMS rotate test, route_decision header present, 2 pilot tenants, runbook for rollback. Also make sure eviction policies for slices are documented (what gets preempted first).

carlo: Small DSL example to include in RFC: `policy: { "priority": ["residency_lock","tenant_affinity","degradation_chain"], "degradation_chain": ["quantized_same_region","compatible_same_region","compatible_other_region"] }`

erin: Action items: Carlo -> written RFC with cost-band estimates and the DSL + decision matrix; Zoe -> ops gate checklist and preflight tests; Samir -> contract snippet + one-pager for sales. I'll coordinate pilots.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket XREG-1132 "cross-region-degradation-playbook: RFC + MVP" assigned carlo. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/XREG-1132

sales-bot: crm-bot: logged pilot interest "AtlasBank EU" and "MarketSignals" for cross-region availability opt-in.

erin: Target to converge in planning sync (ts 4125679100). If we opt for MVP as described we'll unblock 70% of current EU pilots.

carlo: I'll post the RFC by EOD with a dependency graph. Quick note: we should include a small table with example billing adjustments when fallback changes effective latency tiers.

erin: Thanks all :thumbsup:
